posts.headline: Southwest Florida is discounting hardest.
posts.summary: The country's three deepest rent discounts in Q3 2026 were on Florida's Gulf Coast: Naples 12.9%, Fort Myers 11.5% and Sarasota 10.5%, vs 4.2% nationally. In Southwest Florida, asking rent isn't the rent.
posts.alt: Bar chart of Q3 2026 concession rates: Naples 12.9%, Fort Myers 11.5%, Sarasota 10.5%, U.S. 4.2%.

posts.headline: Apartment capital just froze.
posts.summary: All four NMHC October survey indexes fell below 50, with debt financing at 10. 53% of respondents said they can't refinance maturing loans in full without exceeding lender DSCR or LTV limits.
posts.alt: Bar chart of NMHC October 2026 survey indexes vs July: market tightness 47 (57), sales volume 22 (46), equity financing 17 (44), debt financing 10 (46).

posts.headline: Delinquencies are creeping up.
posts.summary: Commercial mortgage delinquencies rose again in Q3 2026: CMBS 4.97%, life companies 1.33% and Fannie/Freddie 1.16%. Distress is building slowly, not breaking.
posts.alt: Bar chart of MBA Q3 2026 delinquency rates vs prior quarter: CMBS 4.97% (4.82), life companies 1.33% (1.19), Fannie and Freddie 1.16% (1.11), FHA 0.90% (1.06).
posts.sourceName: MBA CREF Loan Performance Survey, Q3 2026

posts.headline: Amendment 3 passed.
posts.summary: Florida voters approved Amendment 3 with 62% when the race was called (unofficial). The annual cap on assessed-value increases for non-homestead property, rentals included, drops from 10% to 5% for non-school taxes starting Jan 1, 2027. Informational only, not tax advice.
posts.alt: Graphic showing Florida's non-homestead assessment cap falling from 10% to 5% after Amendment 3 passed with 62% of the vote.

posts.headline: Rent forecasts just went up.
posts.summary: Apartments.com raised its Q4 2027 rent growth forecast to 2.6% from 1.9%, citing demand. October asking rents averaged $1,749, up 1.6% year over year.
posts.alt: Bar chart of Apartments.com's Q4 2027 rent growth forecast rising from 1.9% to 2.6%.

posts.headline: Tampa is still digesting supply.
posts.summary: Tampa effective rents fell 2.5% year over year in Q3 2026 to $1,709, with 7,609 units completed vs 6,859 absorbed over four quarters. Construction starts are down 26%.
posts.alt: Bar chart of Tampa trailing four-quarter completions (7,609) vs net absorption (6,859), Q3 2026.

posts.headline: South Florida's lenders are back.
posts.summary: South Florida rental property loan originations reached $11.8B in Q1–Q3 2026, up 12%, with Fannie/Freddie purchases at $1.4B. September asking rents rose 2.6% in West Palm Beach, 2.0% in Miami and 1.5% in Fort Lauderdale, vs 0.7% nationally.
posts.alt: Bar chart of September 2026 asking rent growth: West Palm Beach 2.6%, Miami 2.0%, Fort Lauderdale 1.5%, U.S. 0.7%.

posts.headline: Rents just turned positive.
posts.summary: Apartment List's national median rent rose 0.1% year over year in October, the first positive reading since mid-2023. Vacancy is 7.0%, still above the 2017–19 average of 6.4%.
posts.alt: Bar chart of October month-over-month rent change: −0.8% in 2025, −0.4% 2017–19 average, −0.3% in 2026.

posts.headline: The 10-year is back at 5%.
posts.summary: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 with two dissents for a hike, and the 10-year Treasury hit 5.05%. The apartment cap rate spread over the 10-year was about 118 bps in Q2, vs a roughly 290 bps average since 2010.
posts.alt: Bar chart comparing the apartment cap rate spread over the 10-year Treasury: about 290 bps average since 2010 vs about 118 bps in Q2 2026.

posts.headline: Florida votes on the apartment tax cap tomorrow.
posts.summary: Amendment 3 would cut the annual cap on assessed-value increases for non-homestead property, rentals included, from 10% to 5% for non-school taxes. Informational only, not a voting recommendation.
posts.alt: Bar chart comparing the current 10% annual cap on non-homestead assessment increases with the proposed 5% cap.

posts.headline: Investors are calling the bottom.
posts.summary: ULI and PwC's Emerging Trends 2027 shows a nearly 5:1 buy-to-hold ratio for multifamily, with deliveries forecast to fall to about 300,000 in 2027.
posts.alt: Bar chart of U.S. apartment deliveries: about 700K at the 2023–24 peak versus about 300K forecast for 2027.

posts.headline: Florida insurance is finally giving back.
posts.summary: The median Florida multifamily property premium per door fell from $797 in early 2025 to $479 in April 2026, while liability premiums are rising.
posts.alt: Bar chart of median Florida multifamily property premium per door: $797 in early 2025 versus $479 in April 2026.

posts.headline: Southwest Florida is still on sale.
posts.summary: Q3 2026 concession rates ran 12.9% in Naples, 11.5% in Fort Myers and 10.5% in Sarasota, versus 4.2% nationally.
posts.alt: Bar chart of Q3 2026 concession rates: Naples 12.9%, Fort Myers 11.5%, Sarasota 10.5%, U.S. average 4.2%.

posts.headline: The supply wave is breaking.
posts.summary: U.S. market-rate completions fell from nearly 588K at the 2024 peak to about 403K in 2025, with roughly 314K forecast for 2026.
posts.alt: Bar chart of U.S. market-rate apartment completions: 588K in 2024, 403K in 2025, 314K forecast for 2026.

posts.headline: Capital just hit the brakes.
posts.summary: All four NMHC October survey indexes came in below 50. The Debt Financing Index fell to 10 from 46 in July.
posts.alt: Bar chart of NMHC October 2026 survey indexes: market tightness 47, sales volume 22, equity financing 17, debt financing 10.

posts.headline: Tampa is digesting the supply wave.
posts.summary: Over the four quarters through Q3 2026, Tampa delivered 7,609 units and absorbed 6,859. Occupancy is 91.8%, and effective rents are down 2.5% year over year.
posts.alt: Bar chart comparing Tampa units delivered (7,609) and absorbed (6,859) over the trailing four quarters.

posts.headline: Apartment CMBS distress just crossed 8%.
posts.summary: Multifamily CMBS delinquency hit 8.04% in September 2026, up from 6.59% a year earlier, and the special servicing rate reached 8.54%.
posts.alt: Column chart of multifamily CMBS delinquency: 6.59% Sep 2025, 7.15% Mar 2026, 8.04% Sep 2026.

posts.headline: 42 of 50 metros blinked in October.
posts.summary: National asking rent fell 0.15% month over month to $1,749 in October 2026, but is still up 1.6% year over year.
posts.alt: Chart showing 42 of the top 50 markets declined in October, with year-over-year rent change for selected metros.

posts.headline: The banks stepped back. Debt funds stepped in.
posts.summary: South Florida rental-housing loan originations hit $11.8B in Q1–Q3 2026. Banks fell to $983M from $1.9B while debt funds lent $3.7B.
posts.alt: Bar chart of South Florida apartment loan volume by lender type: debt funds $3.7B, GSEs $1.4B, banks down to $1.0B.

posts.headline: Orlando is catching its breath.
posts.summary: Construction is down 65.9% from the 2023 peak, and about 6,400 units were absorbed in 2026, outpacing completions for the first time since 2021.
posts.alt: Bar chart of 2021–2026 population growth: Orlando 11.5% vs Miami 6.8%, Palm Beach 6.6%, Fort Lauderdale 5.8%.

posts.headline: $114B in Q3 deals. Look closer.
posts.summary: Q3 apartment sales hit $114.1B, but 61% was entity-level, swollen by the AvalonBay–Equity Residential merger. Without it, volume fell 7% and prices fell 4.6% year over year.
posts.alt: Bar showing 61% of Q3 2026 multifamily volume was entity-level, with declines in volume, single-asset sales and prices.
